title: Associate labels with form controls
description: Form inputs must have programmatically associated labels.

title: Do not use aria-hidden on the document body
description: Ensures the document body is not set to aria-hidden, which would hide the entire page from screen readers.

title: Enable keyboard navigation for all elements
description: All interactive elements are accessible via keyboard with logical focus order and hidden elements excluded from tab sequence.

title: Ensure all input fields have accessible names
description: Checks that input fields have accessible names so screen reader users know what data each field expects.

documentation.title: WAI-ARIA 1.2: Accessible Name and Description Computation

title: Prevent seizure-triggering flashing content
description: Content does not flash more than three times per second to prevent seizures in users with photosensitive epilepsy.

documentation.title: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.3.1: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
W3C: Understanding SC 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold

title: Provide accessible names for buttons
description: All buttons must have a discernible, descriptive accessible name for screen readers.

title: Provide alt text for image buttons
description: Input elements of type='image' must have a descriptive alt attribute.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: Image Button state

title: Support content reflow at 400% zoom
description: Content reflows when zoomed to 400% without requiring horizontal scrolling or loss of functionality.

title: Use logical heading hierarchy
description: Headings follow a sequential structure (h1 to h6) that reflects the content hierarchy without skipping levels.

title: Announce dynamic content with ARIA live regions
description: Dynamic content updates are announced to screen readers using appropriate ARIA live regions.

title: Avoid autoplaying media
description: Audio and video content does not autoplay, or provides immediate controls to pause or stop playback.

title: Avoid redundant entry in the same process
description: Information already provided earlier in a multi-step flow is auto-populated or available for selection instead of being typed again.

title: Avoid sensory-only instructions
description: Instructions do not rely solely on sensory characteristics like color, shape, size, location, or sound.

title: Do not disable pinch zoom
description: The viewport meta tag must not set user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1 as these prevent users from zooming in to read content, violating WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.4 (Resize Text).

documentation.title: Google web.dev: Does not have a <meta name='viewport'> tag with width or initial-scale

title: Ensure ARIA attributes are valid
description: All ARIA attributes must be valid and exist in the WAI-ARIA specification.

title: Ensure ARIA roles contain required child roles
description: Elements with certain ARIA roles must contain the required child roles or the widget structure will be broken for assistive technologies.

title: Ensure content remains usable without CSS
description: Content structure, instructions, and primary tasks remain understandable and operable when author CSS is disabled or replaced by user styles.

documentation.title: W3C: Understanding SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships
MDN: HTML: A good basis for accessibility

title: Ensure logical focus order
description: Tab focus order follows the visual layout and logical reading sequence of the page.

title: Include a skip navigation link
description: A skip navigation link is provided to allow keyboard users to bypass repetitive content and navigate directly to main content.

title: Keep focused elements unobscured
description: Sticky headers, footers, banners, and overlays must not fully hide the element that currently has keyboard focus.

documentation.title: W3C: Understanding SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)

title: Make modal dialogs keyboard accessible
description: Modal dialogs are accessible with proper focus trapping, ARIA attributes, and keyboard dismissal.

title: Manage focus during dynamic interactions
description: Focus is programmatically managed during dynamic interactions like modals, page transitions, and content updates.

title: Meet minimum color contrast ratios
description: Text and background colors must have sufficient contrast to be readable by users with low vision or color blindness.

title: Prevent data loss from session timeouts
description: Users are warned before session expiry, can extend time when appropriate, and can re-authenticate or resume work without losing entered data.

title: Provide accessible authentication methods
description: Authentication flows avoid unnecessary cognitive tests and support assistive mechanisms such as password managers, paste, OTP autofill, and passkeys.

title: Provide accessible names for all interactive elements
description: Checks that interactive elements have accessible names for clear navigation.

title: Provide captions for video content
description: Prerecorded video with audio must have synchronized captions.
detail: Live video must have real-time captions. This is required by WCAG 2.1 SC 1.2.2 and SC 1.2.4.

documentation.title: WebAIM: Captions, Transcripts, and Audio Descriptions

title: Respect reduced motion preferences
description: Animations respect user motion preferences, avoid seizure-triggering flashing, and include warnings for excessive motion.

title: Support both portrait and landscape orientation
description: Content and functionality work in both portrait and landscape unless a specific orientation is essential to the activity.

title: Support text resizing to 200%
description: Text can be resized up to 200% without loss of content or functionality using browser settings.

title: Test with screen readers
description: Pages must be tested with actual screen reader software (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, TalkBack) to verify announcements, focus order, and widget behavior beyond what automated tools can detect.

documentation.title: WebAIM: Using Screen Readers for Testing

title: Use descriptive link text
description: Link text clearly describes the destination or purpose without relying on surrounding context.

title: Use unique IDs for active elements
description: All focusable or active elements must have a unique ID attribute.

title: Use unique IDs for ARIA references
description: IDs referenced by ARIA attributes must be unique to ensure correct accessibility relationships.

title: Align visible labels with accessible names
description: The accessible name of a control should contain its visible label text.

documentation.title: W3C: Understanding SC 2.5.3 Label in Name

title: Allow pasting into form inputs
description: Users should be able to paste content into form fields to improve usability and reduce errors.

title: Avoid focusable descendants in role="text" elements
description: Checks that elements with role='text' have no focusable descendants

title: Avoid meta refresh redirects
description: Meta refresh redirects can disorient users and cause accessibility issues by refreshing the page unexpectedly.

title: Avoid scrolljacking and custom scroll behavior
description: Natural scroll behavior is preserved without custom scroll speeds, directions, or hijacked scroll events.

title: Avoid using deprecated ARIA roles
description: Checks for deprecated or abstract ARIA roles to ensure long-term compatibility.

title: Define proper table headers
description: Checks that data tables have proper headers

title: Ensure accesskey values are unique
description: Checks that accesskey values are unique to avoid shortcut conflicts.

title: Ensure ARIA roles are contained by required parent roles
description: Checks that elements with certain roles have required parent roles

title: Ensure dialogs have an accessible name
description: Checks that dialog elements have accessible names to orient screen reader users.

title: Ensure headings contain text
description: All heading elements (h1-h6) must have visible, descriptive content.

title: Ensure identical links have consistent destinations
description: Links with the same text must point to the same destination or be distinguishable.

documentation.title: W3C: Understanding SC 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)

title: Ensure table headers associate with data cells
description: Checks that table headers have associated data cells

title: Ensure tables have unique accessible names
description: Checks that data tables have unique accessible names

title: Fix empty and broken links
description: All links contain accessible text content and do not lead to broken destinations.

title: Hide decorative elements from assistive technology
description: Decorative images and visual elements are hidden from screen readers using aria-hidden or empty alt attributes.

title: Include required ARIA attributes for roles
description: Checks that elements have required ARIA attributes for their roles

title: Keep repeated help mechanisms in a consistent location
description: When help or support mechanisms appear on multiple pages in the same flow, they stay in the same relative order so users can find them predictably.

title: Link table cells to headers using IDs
description: Checks that td headers attribute references valid th ids

title: Maintain logical heading order
description: Heading levels should follow a sequential, hierarchical order.

title: Make links in text blocks visually distinguishable
description: Links within blocks of text must be distinguishable from surrounding non-link text by more than color alone.

documentation.title: WCAG Technique G183: Using a contrast ratio of 3:1 with surrounding text
WCAG Technique F73: Failure for creating links not visually evident without color vision

title: Match lang and xml:lang attributes
description: The lang and xml:lang attributes on the html element must have identical values to avoid conflicting language signals across HTML and XML parsers.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: The lang and xml:lang attributes

title: Place list items within list containers
description: List item elements (li) must always be direct children of a list container (ul, ol, or menu) to maintain valid HTML structure and correct screen reader announcements.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: The li element

title: Provide accessible names for ARIA command elements
description: Checks that command elements like buttons and links have accessible names for screen reader support.

title: Provide accessible names for meter elements
description: Checks that meter elements have accessible names to provide context for measurements.

title: Provide accessible names for progress bars
description: Checks that progressbar elements have accessible names

title: Provide accessible names for select elements
description: All `<select>` elements must have an associated label or an accessible name to be correctly identified by screen readers.

title: Provide accessible names for toggle fields
description: Checks that toggle fields (checkbox, radio, switch) have accessible names

title: Provide accessible names for tooltips
description: Checks that tooltip elements have accessible names

title: Provide accessible names for tree items
description: All elements with role="treeitem" must have a descriptive accessible name so screen reader users can navigate hierarchical tree widgets.

documentation.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Tree View Pattern

title: Provide alternative text for objects
description: The `<object>` element must contain alternative content to ensure accessibility for users who cannot view the primary content.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: The object element

title: Provide alternatives to parallax effects
description: Parallax scrolling effects have reduced-motion alternatives or can be disabled by users.

title: Provide audio descriptions for video
description: Videos with important visual content include audio descriptions that narrate visual information for blind users.

title: Provide sufficient touch target size
description: Interactive elements must have large enough touch targets so users with motor impairments can activate them accurately on touchscreen devices.

documentation.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Adaptivity and Layout

title: Provide titles for iframes and frames
description: iframes and frames must have a title attribute to describe their content.

title: Remove focusable elements from aria-hidden containers
description: Ensures aria-hidden elements do not contain focusable content to avoid "ghost" focus.

title: Use a single label for each form field
description: Form fields should have exactly one associated <label> element for maximum clarity.

title: Use appropriate tabindex values
description: Checks for appropriate tabindex values

title: Use correct definition list structure
description: Definition lists (<dl>) must only contain valid <dt> and <dd> elements.

title: Use correct list structure
description: Lists (ul, ol) should only contain list item elements (li) to ensure they are correctly interpreted by assistive technology.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: The ul element
HTML Living Standard: The ol element

title: Use exactly one main landmark
description: Each page must have one and only one main landmark.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: The main element

title: Use inclusive language
description: Content uses inclusive, non-discriminatory language that welcomes all users regardless of ability, gender, race, or background.

title: Use landmark regions correctly
description: Proper landmark regions (main, nav, footer) help users navigate the page more efficiently.

title: Use only allowed ARIA attributes for each role
description: Checks that ARIA attributes are allowed on their elements to ensure valid accessibility trees.

title: Use semantic list elements
description: Groups of related items use ul, ol, or dl elements so screen readers announce list context and item count.

title: Use semantic table markup for screen readers
description: Data tables use proper semantic markup with headers, captions, and scope attributes for screen reader accessibility.

title: Use valid ARIA role values
description: Checks for valid ARIA role values

title: Use valid values for ARIA attributes
description: Checks for valid values in ARIA attributes

title: Wrap definition items in a definition list
description: Description terms (<dt>) and details (<dd>) must be contained within a <dl> element.

title: Write in plain language
description: Content uses clear, simple language that is easy to understand for users with cognitive disabilities and non-native speakers.

title: Avoid autofocus on form fields
description: Form fields do not use the autofocus attribute which can disorient screen reader users and cause unexpected page behavior.

title: Avoid images of text
description: Real text is used instead of images containing text, except for logos or when specific visual presentation is essential.

title: Avoid redundant image alternative text
description: Alternative text should not contain redundant words like 'image' or 'photo'.

documentation.title: W3C WAI Images Tutorial: Alternative Text

title: Provide instant anchor scroll option
description: Smooth scroll animations to anchor links respect motion preferences or provide an instant alternative.
